label: Constitutional Analysis
sentences: The question here falls under Article II, Section 3. The President gives Congress information of the state of the Union and recommends measures to it; on extraordinary occasions he may convene both houses or either of them, and if they disagree about the time of adjournment he may adjourn them to such time as he thinks proper; he receives ambassadors and other public ministers, takes care that the laws be faithfully executed, and commissions all the officers of the United States.
This story is about seizing videos while carrying out criminal laws.
In Federalist 69 (March 1788) Hamilton listed the duty "to take care that the laws be faithfully executed" among presidential powers that resemble those of the British king and the New York governor.

On June 1, 1787 Wilson told the Convention that "The only powers he conceived strictly Executive were those of executing the laws, and appointing officers, not appertaining to and appointed by the Legislature."
The FBI used a federal warrant to seize over 900 FaceStealer victim webcam videos.
The strongest argument against this is that this clause only requires the executive to carry out laws already made and does not itself supply power to seize private videos.
We read this clause to mean the executive must carry out the laws that exist.
Seizing videos under a warrant is ordinary execution of criminal law.
This keeps law enforcement separate from law making.

sources.label: James Madison, Notes of Debates in the Federal Convention of 1787, June 1, 1787
